## REQ-PAG-001

**Fields of the PaginationRequest DataSet**

The Payload of a PaginationRequest DataSetMessage contains the mandatory fields PerPage (UInt32 > 0, maximum number of resource DataSetMessages per NetworkMessage of the answer) and Page (UInt32, the requested page); no other field.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Condition: The Get carries a PaginationRequest.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11.1, SF-063
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11.1-79ee4a24, MG-8.3.11.1-83b892c6, MG-8.3.11.1-8cb5f159, MG-8.3.11.1-b256a266

> A published message to the topic method Get may use a PaginationRequest; if it does, the PaginationRequest must contain PerPage.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

> The value of PerPage must be > 0.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

## REQ-PAG-002

**A PaginationRequest is answered page by page**

A Get with a PaginationRequest is answered with NetworkMessages that contain at most PerPage resource DataSetMessages each (helper DataSets not counted). Pages are numbered from 1; page n contains the resource DataSetMessages (n-1)·PerPage+1 … n·PerPage of the result. With Page > 0 only the requested page is published (the requester gets the next page with Page + 1 while HasNext is true); with Page 0 all pages are published one after the other, numbered from 1. A requested page beyond the last page is answered with a page without resource DataSetMessages and HasNext false.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The Get carries a PaginationRequest.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11.1, SF-063
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11.1-35d839fd, MG-8.3.11.1-4d823c40, MG-8.3.11.1-a9803b99, MG-8.3.11.1-b66d8c5d, MG-8.3.11.1-cd18f8ad, MG-8.3.11.1-ce9aec11

> PerPage is the requested page size, i.e. the maximum number of resource DataSetMessages (without helper DataSets such as Pagination or Locale) a NetworkMessage of the related publication may contain.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

> If several NetworkMessages must be published to transport the relevant DataSetMessages, the value of Page shows which page is requested.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

> A requested page beyond the last page must be answered with a page without resource DataSetMessages and HasNext false.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

> The value of Page must be > 0 to get a defined page with related information.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

> The value of Page must be 0 to request all information in a fragmented way with a maximal count of PerPage DataSetMessages for each fragment.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

Notes: Page 0 is no paging through the result but a transmission of the complete result in parts of PerPage DataSetMessages (MG 8.3.11.1). Pages requested with separate Gets are not guaranteed to be consistent (REQ-PAG-007 applies to one series). The publisher may use a smaller page size than requested (REQ-PAG-004).

## REQ-PAG-004

**Pagination values are consistent**

In a Pagination, TotalCount is the number of resource DataSetMessages of the complete result (helper DataSets not counted), PerPage the page size (when answering a PaginationRequest the requested PerPage or a smaller value, e.g. because of the MaxPacketSize), Page the number of the published page starting at 1, HasNext true exactly if Page · PerPage &lt; TotalCount, and PaginationId the MessageId of the first NetworkMessage of the series (the NetworkMessages published for one Get or for one publication not triggered by a Get; an answer for a single page carries its own MessageId). All pages except the last one contain exactly PerPage resource DataSetMessages, the last page may contain fewer.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Condition: The publication carries a Pagination.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11.2, SF-063
- Verification: d7-validate, d7-monitor
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11.2-0e7a1e60, MG-8.3.11.2-1a94fea9, MG-8.3.11.2-2d5655ce, MG-8.3.11.2-3a789a14, MG-8.3.11.2-42fdc31a, MG-8.3.11.2-4b6b231f, MG-8.3.11.2-4eccd43a, MG-8.3.11.2-6fc2b607, MG-8.3.11.2-d6ec42cf, MG-8.3.11.2-e54d779d, MG-8.3.11.2-e698e9f8

> TotalCount is the number of resource DataSetMessages of the complete result (all pages); helper DataSets such as Pagination or Locale are not counted.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> All pages except the last one must contain exactly PerPage resource DataSetMessages; the last page may contain fewer.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> When answering a PaginationRequest, PerPage is the requested PerPage or a smaller value, if the publisher has to limit the page size (e.g. because of the MaxPacketSize, 8.3.11 Pagination).
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> HasNext must be true exactly if Page · PerPage &lt; TotalCount.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> The PaginationId contains the &lt;MessageId> of the first/initial paginated NetworkMessage in this series.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> Therefore, the answer to a Get for a single page contains its own MessageId as PaginationId (B1.1.11 Pagination).
> — MG 8.3.11.2

Notes: Within one NetworkMessage the payload checker verifies the field types, Page ≥ 1, the number of resource DataSetMessages (exactly PerPage, or the rest on the last page, 0 beyond the end), HasNext and – on Page 1 – PaginationId = MessageId; the series (incl. the PaginationId of a single requested page > 1 and a PerPage not above the requested one) is checked by D7 (monitor, test).

## REQ-PAG-005

**Too many DataSetMessages are paginated**

A NetworkMessage does not exceed the MaxPacketSize of the Message Bus (RIG 4.1.1). A publisher that has more resource DataSetMessages than fit into one NetworkMessage (the NetworkMessage would exceed the MaxPacketSize, its own limit for publications not triggered by a Get, or the PerPage of a PaginationRequest) publishes them in several NetworkMessages to the same topic, each with a Pagination, until all DataSetMessages are published. A Get without PaginationRequest is answered with the complete result, paginated if necessary. This applies to every resource published as a list of DataSetMessages (e.g. MAM, Health, Profile, PublicationList, ReferenceDesignation).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.3.11, MG 8.3.11.1, MG 9.1.1, MG 9.1.2, MG 9.1.7, MG 9.1.8, MG 9.1.10, RIG 4.1.1, SF-062, SF-063
- Verification: d7-monitor, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-0a2549a0, MG-8.3.11-135129ca, MG-8.3.11-1d3f1c80, MG-8.3.11-2316f9db, MG-8.3.11-d1b705f1, MG-8.3.11.1-6db49b65, MG-9.1.1-5f90ef30, MG-9.1.1-a242a498, MG-9.1.10-23d0ef72, MG-9.1.10-e685d6ba, MG-9.1.2-0af27f74, MG-9.1.2-262fa218, MG-9.1.3-6a505dc1, MG-9.1.3-7b5c153c, MG-9.1.4-4fa8ccde, MG-9.1.4-82b9abfd, MG-9.1.7-a9a20bff, MG-9.1.7-fe765cc6, MG-9.1.8-03c98043, MG-9.1.8-ea9cd5b6, MG-9.1.9-d64e37b0, MG-9.1.9-d6d5f22d, RIG-4.1.1-5f752b77

> A NetworkMessage must not exceed the MaxPacketSize of the Message Bus (OEC Runtime & Infrastructure Guideline, 4.1.1 Message Bus Storage, at least 262144 bytes).
> — MG 8.3.11

> In this case, it must use the Pagination mechanism.
> — MG 8.3.11

> Pagination information can be used in combination with every Resource that is published as a list of DataSetMessages.
> — MG 8.3.11

> Once too many DataSetMessages are available to add to a single NetworkMessage, pagination mechanism must be used (8.3.11 Pagination).
> — MG 9.1.1

> The publisher must publish as many NetworkMessages to the same topic, using pagination object for telling so, till all DataSetMessages are published.
> — MG 9.1.1

Notes: For publications not triggered by a Get the publisher defines the maximum size on its own (MG 8.3.11), within the MaxPacketSize. The MaxPacketSize of the broker itself is a requirement of the infrastructure (RIG 4.1.1). The pagination sentences of Data and SubscriptionList (MG 9.1.4, 9.1.9) were mapped in C-028, those of Config (MG 9.1.3) in C-029 (inventory only, statement unchanged). The corresponding sentence of RIG 4.1.1 ("A NetworkMessage ... shall not exceed this size") was mapped in C-030 (inventory only).

## REQ-PAG-006

**A subscriber re-triggers a too long publication with PaginationRequest**

An application that cannot handle the size of a publication requests the information again via Get with a PaginationRequest.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber, requester
- Condition: A received publication is too long for the application.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-7898fea4

> If these messages are too long for a specific application, that application must re-trigger publication of the information by using PaginationRequest.
> — MG 8.3.11

## REQ-PAG-007

**Paginated DataSetMessages are consistent**

If NetworkMessages are paginated, the publisher fetches the provided DataSetMessages so that the series is consistent (e.g. a snapshot taken at the start of the series).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Condition: The publication is paginated.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11

## REQ-PAG-008

**PaginationRequest only in Get, Pagination only in Pub**

A NetworkMessage contains a PaginationRequest only with the method Get and a Pagination only with the method Pub, each at most once. A receiver ignores a PaginationRequest or Pagination in a NetworkMessage of another method.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher, requester, responder
- Refs: MG 8.3.11, MG 8.3.11.1, MG 8.3.11.2, SF-062
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-083cc809, MG-8.3.11-f112da9b, MG-8.3.11-f1ca1333

> A PaginationRequest must only be used with the method Get and a Pagination only with the method Pub, each at most once per NetworkMessage.
> — MG 8.3.11

> A PaginationRequest or Pagination in a NetworkMessage of another method is ignored by the receiver.
> — MG 8.3.11

> The Pagination object and PaginationRequest object differ for the methods Pub and Get.
> — MG 8.3.11

> A subscriber that wants to request information via …/Get/&lt;Resource> can add a PaginationRequest object to its payload to define the maximum number of DataSetMessages the NetworkMessage may contain so that the subscriber is able to handle it.
> — MG 8.3.11

Notes: The payload checker reports a misplaced or repeated helper (sender view, strict); a tolerant receiver ignores it (REQ-MSG-046).

## REQ-PAG-009

**Set and Del are not paginated**

Set and Del messages are not paginated: a Set carries a single DataSetMessage addressed by Source and Filter of the topic, a Del none. A single DataSetMessage fits into one NetworkMessage (within the MaxPacketSize).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher, requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.11, SF-062
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-0cb431c2

> A single DataSetMessage must fit into one NetworkMessage; a provider should keep large DataSets well below the MaxPacketSize, e.g. by splitting a large Config into several contexts.
> — MG 8.3.11

Notes: The same sentence recommends (SHOULD) to keep large DataSets well below the MaxPacketSize, e.g. by splitting a large Config into several contexts; the recommendation is covered by this key and not tested separately. Page numbers are no stable addresses (MG 8.3.11), so a Set can not address "page 5" of a large Config (PO review of C-027).
